subject: VPC attachment peering validation & ops metrics

Subject: VPC attachment peering validation & ops metrics

Hi Priya —

Thanks for agreeing to the validation window next week. To make the cutover as low-risk and observable as possible we put together a compact validation runbook and a minimal metrics set we'd like to collect during the attachment exercise. Attached: attachment-validation-playbook.pdf (runbook + command checklist).

High level plan (30-45m):
- Pre-checks (15m): BGP neighbor reachability, ASNs, route filters, MTU verification, port ranges
- Peering bring-up (10m): establish sessions, confirm prefixes advertised, verify route selection on both sides
- Fallback verification (10-15m): exercise WireGuard fallback path we discussed (synchronized routing so control plane traffic still flows if the primary tunnel drops)
- Canary traffic + metrics capture (10m): run small synthetic workload and capture P50/P95 latency, TCP retransmits, and interface errors

Metrics we need from your side (names we expect):
- vpc.peer.bgp.session_state (enum)
- vpc.peer.prefixes_advertised (gauge)
- vpc.peer.rtt_ms{p50,p95} (histogram
- network.tcp_retransmits_total (counter)
- interface.errors_total (counter)

Proposed change window: Tue 2027-05-11, 09:00-10:00 PDT. If that works for you we’ll open a short maintenance notice and our on-call will be standing by.

Quick asks for the configuration snapshot you can attach before the window: acme-peering-config-snapshot.txt — contains BGP neighbor blocks and firewall ACLs (we’ll only review for sanity).

If you want us to run an initial simulated peering test in staging beforehand, we can do that Wednesday.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for the clear plan and the runbook. Tue 2027-05-11 09:00 PDT works for our network window. A couple of clarifying asks from our side before the runbook run: 

1) Can you confirm expected MTU and whether we should explicitly set TCP MSS on the edge devices for the WireGuard fallback path? We’ve seen fragmentation issues when a fallback tunnel adds extra overhead.
2) Are you expecting us to terminate the WireGuard at the same edge routers or at a separate HA pair? That affects stateful ACL design.
3) For metrics collection: we will need the exact metric names so our telemetry team can map them into our Grafana dashboard. If you can paste the Prometheus scrape job snippet that would be ideal.

I attached a preliminary config snapshot for your review (will send the full one in a follow-up after a quick scrub). We’ll also loop in our Security Ops during the window — their alias is ops-eng@acme-corp.com.

—Priya
Priya Shah
Network Program Manager, Acme Corp
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: VPC attachment peering validation & ops metrics

Thanks Priya — good questions, answered inline: 

On Wed, May 5, 2027 at 10:03 AM Priya Shah <priya.shah@acme.com> wrote:
> 1) Can you confirm expected MTU and whether we should explicitly set TCP MSS on the edge devices for the WireGuard fallback path?

We recommend MTU 1500 on the physical interfaces and an effective path MTU of 1400 for encapsulated tunnels (WireGuard ~ overhead). Yes, configure TCP MSS clamp to 1360 on the egress ACLs for the fallback path to avoid fragmentation on mixed path flows.

> 2) Are you expecting us to terminate the WireGuard at the same edge routers or at a separate HA pair?

Prefer terminating on the HA pair dedicated for customer attachments (same datacenter pair). That keeps control-plane separation clear.

> 3) For metrics collection: we will need the exact metric names so our telemetry team can map them into our Grafana dashboard. If you can paste the Prometheus scrape job snippet that would be ideal.

Prometheus snippet (paste into your scrape config):
- job_name: 'acme-vpc-peering'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['10.10.1.12:9100']  # replace with your exporter endpoint
  metrics_path: '/metrics'
  labels:
    env: 'prod'

I’ve attached a minimal config snapshot (acme-peering-config-snapshot.txt). We’ll also publish a lightweight alert rule for elevated TCP retransmits and bgp session flaps.

Schedule: Tue 2027-05-11 09:00-09:30 PDT (plan + prechecks), 09:30-09:45 PDT (peering bring-up), 09:45-09:55 PDT (fallback exercise), 09:55-10:00 PDT (canary verification).

We’ll open JIRA-RED-1427 to capture follow-ups and the post-run checklist.

—Karthik
